The town itself, from the extent of its popu- lation, its celebrity as a place of summer resort, the increasing number of its shipping, and the amount of its trade, would fully justify the attempt to establish some local organ of communication; but in addition to this the extensive mining district around us evidently requires a medium by whif||its claims may be advocated, and its local interests upheld if towns of less extent and importance have their newspaper, it seems, unreasonable that Aberystwith Should not keep pace with the advancing spirit of the age; therefore we propose to offer to ^he inhabitants of this district a journal whicfi "ShaH^be ej^ciu^ely their "« n. j Bnt what is it to contain V w ,i í Allo* us, first, to say what it cuntam. The preaching was effective and edifying; and the hearers, of whom many had come from a great dis- tance, departed, feeling it was well for them to have I been present. PETTY SESSIONS.-At the Town Hall, on Tuesday last, before F. R. Roberts, Esq (Mayor,) and D. Edwards, Esq., J.P. Adam Lewis, Marine Store Dealer, was brought up, charged by P. C. Evaas^ with being on Friday, the 11th inst., drunk and disorderly, and resisting the police in the execution of their duty. p. C. Evans being sworn said, that he saw the prisbuer on that day by the Meat Mar- ket very drunk and noisy. He resisted very much- when being taken to custody. The prisoner called several witnesses to prove -that he was not at the t time disorderly. The Mayor addressing the prison- rfri*% that this.^aatlie third or fourth time he bad oSsTi DiWght up befort1^^—.[he Jast time not later than a month ago; and .lie ,er well knew that this sort of* conduct COufq not be tolerated. He hoped this case Would be a waruing to hivn, and would now inflict a ifne of 10s. and costs*, adding that should the prisoner ever be again brought before him, he should infliet a penalty to the greatest extent allowed by law. COMMISSIONERS' MEETING—At the Town Hall, on Tuesday last, an adjourned meeting was held. Present, Jno. M. Davies, Esq., (in the chair,) Messrs. C. Hackney, R. Morris, T. Cleaton, E. W. Jones, J. Jenkins, P. Williams, T. Jones, D.Jones, J. E. Jones, J^Lpnes, GreatBark-gflteSt.. J. Rees, J .Jones, Princess St., R. Watkins, G. Morice, and J. Leon. Several bills were examined, passed, and ordered to be paid. IQanswer to a question pat, theJTcrmJ»fi^t >«<Md that the cost incurred in the tnafaSng of the new reservoir would be under £ 90. Mr. Hackney spoke in high terms of the manner In which the Turncock nad completed the same, Mr. Leon remarking tliat, as a token of their apprbbation, he should propose to vote for him a set of China service. (Laughter.) On the motion of Mr. Cleaton, jE2 was allowed the Tarncoek for the services which he said his son had rendered him whilst at work at the reservoir. The reservoir committee were requested to wait upon Mr. Richardes, Penglaise, and ask permission to be allowed to turn the water, which now ran through his garden on Rhi wlais, in another direction. Three tenders were received from persons desirous^ of contracting for sweeping and cleansing the streels for the ensuing year. That of Edward Jones, the present contractor, for jE80, was accepted. Mr. Watkins complained of dung beaps being al- lowed to remain in Sandmarsh road. The scaven- ger was ordered to remove the same. Mr. Hackney was shocked with the state of things in Prospect c Row. He was certain the scavenger had not seen the place for a week or a fortnight. Matters were equally bad in Crynfryn Row—pigstyes met the eye in different quarters, to say nothing of nuisances of a still worse description. Mr. Watkins said it was M&beer neglect on the part of the surveyor to allow the places mentioned1 to be in the state described. The meeting afterward-, broke up. THUNDER STOItM.-On Tuesday evening, the 8th instant, this place was visited by a thunder stonn, which continued without intermission during the whoie of We night. The lightning were most vivid, accompanied occasionally? by heavy sMowers of rain. We are happy to ttate, however, that we have to record no accident having occurred in this town or vicinity. Anothej violent thunderstorm broke over tljis place andv neighbourhood 'on Friday, the 1 lift instant. It ("e«HlreQpefi--a*fiut 6 o'clock, and lasted with unabated fury the whole of the?night. The flashes of lightning weffe most vivid, and the peals Of-tfetirjder at one time terrific. In the neighbour- hood of Ystumtuen and Pontferwyd the electric fluid did some mischief. Near the former place several sheep and tambs, were killed. It appears that so dazzling was the lightning, and so. loud the thunder, that the flock ot sheep was alsrftned and rushed to one corner of the field. Whilst thus huddled together, some of them were struck by the lightning, and killed on the spot.
